summary: railway.ts has been type-checked and evaluated locally but `railway config plan` has never run against it
detail: `plan` needs a linked Railway project, which the session that wrote this did not have. What is checked: tsc accepts the file, and evaluating it gives a service with a volume attachment at /data. What is not: whether the engine wants the volume listed in `resources` as well as attached with `volumeMounts` (the SDK's own graph code does not say; the attachment carries its own volume config), and that the build and start commands deploy. Run `railway config plan` on a real project and show the result before the first apply.

summary: The evolve skill's steps were each applied to a scratch copy and run, but nothing in this repo fails if one goes stale
detail: Step 2 (a WebSocket) was applied from the skill's own code blocks to a copy of the app (27 tests at 100%), and step 3 (a delta document) to another (21 tests at 100%, a second window sees a save, typing is not overwritten). summary: shinko is meant to become a resource, perhaps a flavour of delta: a realtime shared tree with formulas
detail: Peter, 3 Oct: shinko is just another resource, a realtime shared tree, and it should evolve into one, perhaps as a flavour of delta. It is work in progress, so the evolve skill only names it and has no section for it yet. Things found while looking: shinko is a private repo and not on npm ("private": true), so `bun add github:blueshed/shinko` answers 404 without a token. It serves a person over a Bun WebSocket (`serve`, with `foreign` and `sending`), and a page uses `connect` from `shinko/client`; `examples/socket.ts` and `examples/echo` are the smallest hosts. Two questions for when it is a resource: its socket next to the app's `/ws` (Bun.serve has one websocket handler, so the two need telling apart by ws.data, or one socket carries both), and installing it.
note: 2026-10-03: added. Not built, at Peter's direction.

summary: duckdown's bun-create postinstall is "bun run create/setup.ts", which bun create runs with a second `bun run` in front: nothing happens
detail: Found building paintbrush's create script. bun create prefixes every postinstall entry with `bun run`, so an entry that starts with `bun run` does nothing, silently. Checked on Bun 1.4.2 by running duckdown's own create from a local copy (BUN_CREATE_DIR): the created site kept the template's todo.jsonl and create/, and had no site/. The entry that works is create/setup.ts. The GitHub path was not run, but Bun's docs say it shares the steps. duckdown's ledger and README are the home for this; it is noted here so the finding is not lost.
note: 2026-10-02: found; not yet told to duckdown. Open, for Peter.

summary: The web sandbox hook is railroad's, adapted, and has not been run in a Claude Code web session
detail: railroad's hook is written from what was found out in that sandbox (an older base-image Bun, no browser, the browser download hosts blocked, npm and GitHub reachable) and its CLAUDE.md says it works there. This copy changes one thing: the Bun floor is read from engines.bun in package.json instead of a constant. What is checked here: bash accepts it, and a test shows it does nothing when CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is not set. The Linux half of the problem is covered by CI, which ran green on the pull request: Bun 1.4.2 from package.json, Chrome wrapped with --no-sandbox, the browser tests passing. What is not checked: a run with CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true in a real web session, which would also show whether Bun 1.4 installs through npm there.
